```
143	## Phase 1 — Earned patches (the core rework)
144	
145	Replace the blind seed patch with a patch **grown face-by-face under
146	validation**, promoting the surface type as the accumulated support allows.
147	Full design + math in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN ("The Robustness Rework", Phase 1
148	design). Commit semantics deliberately unchanged: earned (type, params,
149	patch) hands off to the existing \`grow_from\` flood/refit path, and every
150	commit gate (\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, torus ratio, \`MIN_*_FACES\`,
151	\`resolve_claims\`) keeps its exact meaning.
152	
153	- **1.1 Closed-form initializers, unit-tested first** (synthetic strips/tori;
154	  the corpus's exactness precedents — r = 0.99998-style — make ~1e-9
155	  assertions appropriate):
156	  - Cylinder: axis = n₁ × n₂ from two admitted faces with non-parallel
157	    normals (exact on strip/quad tessellation), then \`fit_circle_for_axis\`
158	    (cylindrical.rs — exists, measured well-conditioned on 40–65° arcs).
159	    Guard with a numeric conditioning floor on |n₁×n₂|, documented as
160	    validity-not-threshold.
161	  - Sphere: normal lines anchored at facet **circumcenters** (exact through
162	    the centre for inscribed facets); centre = common-perpendicular midpoint
163	    of two lines; radius = mean distance.
164	  - Cone: existing normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
165	    (\`smallest_eigenvector_3x3\`) + \`axis_normals_consistent\`.
166	  - Torus (**time-boxed — skip without blocking the phase if conditioning
167	    fails**): axis from the meridian-coplanarity system
168	    \`(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0\` over ≥4 faces (bilinear; solve by alternation or
169	    pairwise elimination; rank-deficient on sphere/cylinder data by
170	    construction — ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede it);
171	    then (R, r) via the existing \`fit_circle_2d\` profile fit (toroidal.rs).
172	- **1.2 The earn loop.** Replace \`seed_patch\` + \`condition_patch\` inside
173	  \`grow\` (compete.rs): BFS from the seed; admit a frontier face iff it
174	  validates the current fit at vtol (\`face_validates\`); on failure attempt
175	  **promotion** in ladder order (plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus),
176	  refitting accepted+candidate and requiring **all already-accepted faces**
177	  to validate under the promoted fit; if nothing validates, the face is
178	  across a seam — exclude it and **record it as a frontier face** (Phase 2
179	  consumes these). **Branch on ambiguity** (e.g. two same-height cylinder
180	  faces validating as a sphere): grow both; false branches should self-prune
181	  within ~2 faces. Hand each surviving (type, patch, params) to the unchanged
182	  \`grow_from\`. Add counters (behind verbosity/env): NO-GROWTH count, branches
183	  spawned / died-within-2, promotions attempted/accepted, frontier faces.
184	- **1.3 Drift-triggered cylinder→torus promotion** (time-boxed). A bend is
185	  locally a valid cylinder, so admission never fails; the signal is
186	  **sign-consistent precession** of the fitted axis across successive refits
187	  as support accumulates — not a magnitude test (if a magnitude constant
188	  seems needed, stop and ask). If it works, \`promote_bend\` + \`BEND_*\` become
189	  Phase-4 deletion candidates; if not, keep them and move on.
190	- **1.4 Validate.**
191	  - *Initializer accuracy per provenance*: measure cylinder-axis error vs
192	    references across Parasolid strips AND the Phase-0 OCCT Delaunay meshes.
193	    If median error exceeds ~1° on a provenance, degrade that provenance to
194	    the covariance axis over the earned patch (still clean, still not blind).
195	    **Stop and ask** if even that underperforms the blind patch anywhere.
196	  - *Branch lifetime*: if branches persist past ~2 faces, validation is less
197	    sharp than believed — stop and ask before the cost model changes.
198	  - *NO-GROWTH count* (baseline 323 on stepped_block fine) should collapse
199	    toward zero.
200	  - *Acceptance*: probe per-type breakdowns equal-or-better corpus-wide;
201	    stepped_block fine ≥ today's 75-surface state; **stepped_block medium and
202	    part_rounded_cube coarse not worse** (the identifiability stress cases —
203	    the one place the blind patch did irreplaceable work); suite green;
204	    harness ≥ baseline.
205	- **1.5 Delete after ablation** (rule 4): \`condition_patch\`, \`seed_patch\`'s
206	  jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`, \`PATCH_RADII\`,
207	  \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`; likely \`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\`.
208	  Report the constant count.
209	
210	**Explicitly NOT fixed by this phase — do not chase here**: stepped fine's 4
211	surplus surfaces, medium's remaining gap, hill_with_hole's junk torus

217	
218	- **2.1 Profile first.** Instrument the stepped_block fine run (103 s
219	  baseline): time in earn/patch construction vs LM fits vs floods vs
220	  \`resolve_claims\`. Report the split to the user. **Only build 2.2–2.4 if the
221	  seed sweep dominates**; otherwise apply the cheapest fix the profile names.
222	- **2.2 Distance field + farthest-first seeding.** Per-face geodesic distance
223	  to the region boundary (multi-source Dijkstra over face adjacency,
224	  **centroid-gap weights in mm, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded
225	  meshes). Order seeds farthest-first, replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\`.
226	- **2.3 Duplicate abort.** Skip a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely
227	  inside one committed surface (it can only refit that surface) — the
228	  topological generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`; no numeric tolerance.

230	  1's excluded frontier faces as new distance sources incrementally — the

340	## Reserve — partition-level architecture (user sign-off required)
341	
342	If, **as measured by the harness**, Phases 1–4 leave seeding quality or sweep
343	cost unacceptable, the remaining lever is replacing the per-face sweep with a
344	partition: recursive split-and-merge (earned-patch fits at nodes,
345	union-revalidate merges via \`fit_validate\`, identifiability guards becoming
346	"defer, don't reject" until merge time) and/or VSA-style global alternation.
347	Both are deliberately reserved: they rewrite known-working machinery
348	(\`resolve_claims\`, relabel, merge) and their known hard parts (cut lines vs
349	seams; inverted identifiability) are documented in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN
350	("Considered and not adopted"). **Do not start without bringing Phase 1–4
351	measurements to the user.**
```

```
1666	## The Robustness Rework (2026-07-29)
1667	
1668	**This section is the rationale behind the phased plan in TODO.md.** TODO.md
1669	carries the step-by-step instructions; this section records why each phase is
1670	shaped the way it is, the design detail for the two new mechanisms (earned
1671	patches, distance-guided exploration), the corpus strategy, what was considered
1672	and deliberately not adopted, and the measurements preserved from the TODO
1673	items the plan retired. It synthesizes two parallel design sessions held
1674	2026-07-29 (one logged at \`agent-logs/2026-07-29_14-59_nothinking.md\`) plus the
1675	measured record above.
1676	
1677	### Goal and thesis
1678	
1679	The goal changed: **maximum robustness and minimum fragility over all plausible
1680	CAD-derived meshes**, not score on the current corpus. Fragility is
1681	operationalized as two headline numbers: the stage-2 tuned-constant count
1682	(34 at plan time; \`grep -h "^const \|^pub(crate) const \|^pub(super) const "
1683	src/stage2/*.rs | wc -l\`) and the **cliff count** — the number of constants
1684	whose ±2× perturbation collapses any model (four unrelated knobs once each
1685	flipped stepped_block medium from 83 surfaces to full per-facet collapse).
1686	
1687	The measured fragility concentrates in three structural debts, and the plan
1688	retires them in dependency order:
1689	
1690	1. **Evaluation is anecdotal.** 14 hand-watched models, Onshape/Parasolid-heavy;
1691	   three NURBS models rotted silently because nothing watched them. You cannot
1692	   claim generality you cannot measure → Phase 0 builds the instrument first.
1693	2. **Two of three tolerances are guesses.** \`--surface-tolerance\` defaults to
1694	   0.4 mm against a measured true sag of ~9e-4 mm (~400× too loose), making
1695	   centroid validation nearly vacuous; \`--angular-tolerance\` is a stand-in for
1696	   a discarded exporter setting. Both are measurable from the mesh itself
1697	   → Phases 0 (diagnostics) and 3 (regime flip).
1698	3. **One component — blind-patch seeding — forces most of the guard pile.**
1699	   \`seed_patch\`/\`condition_patch\` fit an unvalidated 32-face BFS neighbourhood;
1700	   the contamination lives on in the fit parameters, producing both the 323
1701	   NO-GROWTH seeds and plausible-but-wrong fits. Roughly two-thirds of stage
1702	   2's constants exist because tangent seams are invisible to it → Phases 1–2
1703	   replace the mechanism, Phase 4 deletes what that makes inert.
1704	
1705	Everything else measured principled — stage 1, sharp-edge regions, the DOF
1706	ladder, \`fit_validate\`, \`face_validates\`, flood, \`resolve_claims\`,
1707	relabel+refit, the locus machinery, stage 3 topological assembly, the
1708	\`--compare\` gates — **is deliberately not touched**.
1709	
1710	### Phase 1 design: earned patches (replaces the blind patch)
1711	
1712	Replace grab-then-repair with **grow-under-validation**: BFS from the seed,
1713	admitting a frontier face only if it validates against the current fit at
1714	vertex tolerance; when a face fails, attempt **promotion** up the ladder
1715	(plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus), refitting accepted+candidate and
1716	requiring *every already-accepted face* to still validate; if no type
1717	validates, the face is across a seam — exclude it and record it as a
1718	**frontier face** (Phase 2 consumes these). The patch can never straddle a
1719	junction by construction, which is the exact property the blind patch lacks.
1720	Commit semantics do not change: the earned (type, params, patch) goes to the
1721	unchanged \`grow_from\` flood/refit path, and every existing commit gate
1722	(\`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\`, torus ratio, \`MIN_*_FACES\`, \`resolve_claims\`) keeps
1723	its meaning.
1724	
1725	What makes promotion workable at tiny support — where a free least-squares fit
1726	is hopeless (sagitta arithmetic: over a 7.5° arc on r = 0.5 the sag is
1727	~0.001 mm against a 2e-5 mm quantum, so a free radius is ~2% ≈ 200× vtol
1728	wrong) — is that **facet normals are exact** and give closed-form,
1729	DOF-reducing initializers:
1730	
1731	- **Cylinder — axis = n₁ × n₂.** A planar facet spanning two rulings of a
1732	  cylinder has its normal exactly perpendicular to the axis, at any coarseness,
1733	  so two facets with non-parallel normals give the axis exactly on
1734	  strip/quad-tessellated surfaces. Radius+origin then come from
1735	  \`fit_circle_for_axis\` (cylindrical.rs), measured well-conditioned on short
1736	  arcs (r = 0.99998 / 0.99999 / 0.50008 from 65°/60°/40° arcs). **Provenance
1737	  caveat:** a general Delaunay triangle's normal is *not* exactly
1738	  perpendicular to the axis; measure axis error per provenance (Phase 0's OCCT
1739	  meshes), and degrade to the normal-covariance axis over the earned patch
1740	  where needed — still clean, still not blind.
1741	- **Sphere — concurrent normal lines.** For any planar facet inscribed in a
1742	  sphere, the line through the facet's **circumcenter** along its normal
1743	  passes exactly through the sphere centre (equidistance). Two facets → centre
1744	  at the near-intersection (common-perpendicular midpoint), radius = distance.
1745	- **Cone** — the existing normal-covariance axis (\`smallest_eigenvector_3x3\`)
1746	  over the earned patch, guarded by \`axis_normals_consistent\`, both existing.
1747	- **Torus — meridian coplanarity, the "open case" closed.** Every torus
1748	  normal line lies in the meridian plane through its point, which contains
1749	  the axis — so each facet contributes one coplanarity constraint
1750	  \`(pᵢ − a) · (nᵢ × d) = 0\` on the axis (point a, direction d; 4 DOF; the
1751	  system is bilinear — solve by alternation or pairwise elimination). Four
1752	  facets pin the axis; then (R, r) is a 2-D circle fit in (ρ, z) profile
1753	  coordinates — \`fit_circle_2d\` already exists (toroidal.rs). **Caveats:**
1754	  rank-deficient by construction on sphere data (any axis through the centre
1755	  satisfies it) and consistent-but-degenerate on cylinder data, so ladder
1756	  order and a conditioning floor must precede it; grid-aligned quads give
1757	  near-exact meridian normals, Delaunay triangles do not. **Time-boxed**: unit
1758	  test to ~1e-9 on synthetic tori before integrating; if conditioning does not
1759	  pan out, skip it — direct torus seeding stays as today and Phase 1 is not
1760	  blocked.
1761	
1762	Two behaviours need more than validation failure:
1763	
1764	- **Ambiguity → branch, don't choose.** Two same-height faces of a cylinder
1765	  validate as a sphere centred on the axis (the hole→sphere trap at patch
1766	  scale). Grow both branches; the false one should die within a face or two
1767	  (the next face at a different height is off the sphere by ≈ Δ²/2R ≫ vtol).
1768	  Instrument branch lifetime; persistent branches mean validation is less
1769	  sharp than believed — stop and ask.
1770	- **Bent tube → drift-triggered promotion.** A bend is locally a valid
1771	  cylinder (sag of the bend over a 2 mm patch at R = 14 is ~3.6e-5 mm), so
1772	  admission never fails and promotion never triggers on residual. The signal
1773	  is **systematic fit drift**: along a straight tube successive refits are
1774	  stationary; along a bend the fitted axis precesses with a consistent sign as
1775	  support accumulates. Test drift as sign-consistency of successive axis
1776	  deltas, *not* magnitude (a magnitude bar would be a new tuned constant —
1777	  stop and ask if one seems needed). Success retires \`promote_bend\` and the
1778	  \`BEND_*\` constants; failure keeps them, and that is fine.
1779	
1780	**Deleted when this lands (after ablation evidence):** \`condition_patch\`
1781	entirely, \`seed_patch\`'s jet filtering, \`SEED_PATCH_CAP\`, \`MAX_PATCH_DEPTH\`,
1782	\`PATCH_RADII\`, \`PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS\`, \`MIN_CONDITION_FACES\`, likely
1783	\`MAX_TORUS_STARTS\` (multiple flood starts exist because the fit patch was
1784	unreliable).
1785	
1786	### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration
1787	
1788	The 26122-face seed sweep costs 103 s on stepped_block fine and its
1789	useful-work fraction is unknown (profile first — do not build this phase's
1790	machinery if the profile says the cost is in fits or floods rather than the
1791	sweep). The principled orderings and bounds, all derived rather than tuned:
1792	
1793	- **Distance field**: per-face geodesic distance to the region boundary
1794	  (multi-source Dijkstra over the dual graph, **centroid-gap weights in
1795	  millimetres, not hops** — hop counts lie on graded meshes, which is what
1796	  \`PATCH_RADII\` existed to patch). Seed **farthest-first** (Gonzalez maximin),
1797	  replacing \`neighbor_jet_mismatch\` — the jet-based proxy for exactly this
1798	  quantity.
1799	- **Feedback, not detection**: tangent junctions cannot be *detected* (the
1800	  measured-dead pivot; a tangent junction is locally the *smoothest* place on
1801	  the mesh — an anti-edge), but they are *discovered exactly* by Phase 1's
1802	  excluded frontier faces. Add discovered frontiers as new distance sources
1803	  incrementally. The only trustworthy edge map is the one the fits produce.
1804	- **Duplicate abort**: a seed whose reachable ball lies entirely inside one
1805	  committed surface can only refit that surface — skip it. Topological, a
1806	  strict generalization of \`interior_of_claims\`, no numeric tolerance.
1807	- **Acceptance discipline**: ordering must not change results. Bit-identical
1808	  probe output, or every diff explained; order-dependence is itself the
1809	  fragility being removed — stop and surface it.
1810	
1811	### Phase 0 design: the corpus and the instrument
1812	
1813	Three provenance sources, cheapest first, all scored against reference STEPs:
1814	
1815	1. **OCCT re-mesh of existing references** (automated, free ground truth).
1816	   \`gen_test_models\` already drives \`BRepMesh\` with deflection/angle settings
1817	   (\`write_tessellated_stl\`); add a mode that loads any reference STEP and
1818	   emits STL variants at several settings, plus **off-origin variants**
1819	   (translate the shape ~1 m before both STL and STEP output) so the float32
1820	   quantum question becomes testable. This adds constrained-Delaunay
1821	   provenance to a strip-heavy corpus.
1822	2. **Fusion 360 re-export** (user batch job): import reference STEPs, export
1823	   STL at low/medium/high. Different tessellator, same ground truth.
1824	3. **Wild STEP+STL pairs** (most representative, most care): harvest models
1825	   published with both a STEP/F3D and an STL (Thingiverse API / Printables /
1826	   GrabCAD, scripted or via a browser session). **Pair-verification gate**:
1827	   run stage 1 \`--compare\`; a pair counts as ground truth only if mesh
1828	   vertices lie on the STEP surfaces to within a few quanta — otherwise
1829	   quarantine as crash-test-only (the STL may be a different revision,
1830	   decimated, or repaired). Record the verification *rate*: it is itself the
1831	   first field measurement of the provenance premise ("vertices lie on the
1832	   true surface") in the wild. Keep licensing clean: store source URL,
1833	   author, license, and hash in a manifest; do not commit files whose license
1834	   does not permit redistribution (gitignore the external corpus, commit the
1835	   manifest).
1836	
1837	The instrument: a one-command sweep harness (per-model rows: per-type surface
1838	breakdown, \`--compare\` distances, volume error, runtime, exit status;
1839	machine-readable; saved baselines + diff mode) and a **fragility meter** that
1840	perturbs/ablates each stage-2 constant and reports which models change.
1841	
1842	### Tolerance sequencing (Phases 0 and 3)
1843	
1844	Estimators are built and *reported* in Phase 0 (they double as the
1845	provenance-violation detector: estimator disagreement or a missing dihedral
1846	gap means a decimated/remeshed/faceted-by-construction input — warn now,
1847	degrade gracefully in Phase 6). The **default flip is deferred to Phase 3**,
1848	after the seeding rework stabilizes: a 400× change to \`stol\` moves behaviour
1849	everywhere (\`REFIT_GIVE_UP\` is 8×stol; merge gates and \`face_validates\` use
1850	it), and debugging it concurrently with new seeding would confound both. The
1851	earn loop admits on *vertex* tolerance, so Phase 1 is essentially independent
1852	of the stol regime. Ablation (Phase 4) runs after the flip so deletions are
1853	judged under the final regime.
1854	
1855	### Considered and not adopted (with reasons)
1856	
1857	- **Recursive subdivision / split-and-merge as the architecture.** Strong
1858	  asymptotics (the tree visits only boundary-containing paths) and its merge
1859	  half already exists (\`fit_validate\` as union-revalidation), but: fixed
1860	  geometric cuts do not respect seams (boundaries are mesh-edge chains;
1861	  strip-shaped surfaces stay contaminated at every level until cells are
1862	  smaller than the strip), and identifiability *inverts* — a sub-node of a
1863	  real torus legitimately sweeps 5° and fits garbage parameters that validate
1864	  locally, so every sweep guard would need to become "defer, don't reject"
1865	  until merge time, a rework of commit semantics. Phases 1–2 deliver most of
1866	  its benefit at a fraction of the risk. **Held in reserve**; do not start
1867	  without Phase 1–4 measurements in hand and user sign-off.
1868	- **Precomputed junction-evidence field for seeding** (dihedral
1869	  second-difference, diffused; or any jet/dihedral edge map). Any field
1870	  computed *before* fitting is a detector prior — the refuted detector
1871	  returning in a hat. Superseded by the exact, threshold-free fit-derived
1872	  frontier field of Phase 2. (For the record, the raw idea also had a real
1873	  basis: within a tessellated surface the dihedral field is locally
1874	  consistent and *steps* at junctions — but the OCCT-Delaunay and
1875	  coarse-mesh cases erode it, and nothing needs it once frontiers exist.)
1876	- **The "bridge" formulation of type promotion** (grow under an
1877	  exactly-determined uncommittable fit until the new DOF identify). Correct
1878	  shape, but its fragile middle regime — junction faces soaking into
1879	  exactly-determined fits — is mostly obviated by the closed-form
1880	  initializers, which pin the new DOF geometrically at 2–4 faces instead of
1881	  waiting for least-squares identifiability. The earn loop keeps the bridge's
1882	  two sound rules: full-support revalidation on every accretion, and
1883	  identifiability-gated *commits*.
1884	- **VSA (the old item C)** as a planned phase. Earned patches + the existing
1885	  relabel/refit fixpoint already implement the alternation locally, and the
1886	  known-working machinery it would replace (\`resolve_claims\`, relabel, merge)
1887	  is exactly what a big rewrite puts at risk. Reserve, same gate as
1888	  subdivision. The pending \`snap_boundaries\` keep/delete decision folds into
1889	  Phase 4 with fresh ablation data (it is the per-face assignment criterion a
1890	  future VSA would need, and the locus diagnostic depends on the module).
1891	- **Retuning anything to close the last corpus gaps first** (stepped fine's 4
1892	  surplus surfaces, medium's ~13). Deliberately deferred: they are boundary-
1893	  and identifiability-residue that Phases 1–4 either fix or isolate, and
1894	  chasing them now re-enters the one-model-at-a-time loop that produced the
1895	  fragility.
1896
```

```
             END{printf "%d/%d/%d/%d/%d/%d", p+0,c+0,k+0,s+0,t+0,b+0}')
  printf "%-17s %s\n" "$(basename $m | cut -c1-17)" "$b"
done
```

```
use brepper::{config, stage1, stage2, stage3, stage4};

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn config_for_output(stl_path: &str, output_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "-o", output_path, "-q"]).unwrap()
}

fn config_for_compare(stl_path: &str, output_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config = config::parse_config_from([
        "brepper", stl_path, "-o", output_path, "--compare", step_path, "-q",
    ])
    .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

fn run_stage4(config: &config::Config) {
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(config).expect("stage1 should pass");
    let surfaces = stage2::stage2(config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass");
    let brep = stage3::stage3(config, surfaces, None).expect("stage3 should pass");
    stage4::stage4(config, brep).expect("stage4 should pass");
}

// --- Basic STEP output tests ---

    let dir = manifest_dir();
    let stl = format!("{dir}/tests/ccad/generated/cube.stl");

    run_stage4(&config);
    assert!(std::path::Path::new(&out).exists());
}
```

```
    Before this the eight NURBS models had stage-2 selection tests and

    regresses them is visible rather than silent.

    correct 7 are all present and exact; the surplus is a single junk torus
    of 17 faces, R=3.5101 r=2.3882, area 1.533 mm2, carved out of the

    SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES = 16, and its r/R of 0.680 sits just under
    MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO = 0.7.

    quantity not among the four count-based candidacy rules already measured
    wrong, and one that diverges from count by orders of magnitude on a strip
    mesh. The junk torus is 0.095% of its freeform patch's area while
    cone_tangent_planes' real cones, which broke every previous rule, are a
    large fraction of theirs. TODO says to measure that separation across the
    corpus first, and to re-check cone_tangent_planes and the elliptical
    models specifically.
    
    Suite 513 passing / 9 ignored.
```

```
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// NURBS corpus: end-to-end --compare
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// Added 2026-07-28. Before this the NURBS models had stage-2 *selection* tests
+// and nothing end to end, which is how three of the eight came to be silently

+
+macro_rules! nurbs_compare {
+    ($name:ident, $model:literal) => {

+                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.stl", $model),

+            run_stage4(&config);

+    };
+    ($name:ident, $model:literal, ignore = $why:literal) => {
+        #[test]

+            let config = config_for_compare(

+                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_nurbs_{}.step", $model),
+                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.step", $model),

+        }
```

```
472	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
473	// NURBS corpus: end-to-end --compare
474	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
475	//
476	// Added 2026-07-28. Before this the NURBS models had stage-2 *selection* tests
477	// and nothing end to end, which is how three of the eight came to be silently
478	// broken: \`bspline_blister\` and \`bspline_saddle\` had collapsed to all-per-facet
479	// polyhedra and \`hill_with_hole\` was being shredded into 47 surfaces against a
480	// reference 7, all unnoticed because only stage 1 was checked. Every model has
481	// a reference STEP sitting next to it, so there was never a reason not to.
482	
483	macro_rules! nurbs_compare {
484	    ($name:ident, $model:literal) => {
485	        #[test]
486	        fn $name() {
487	            let dir = manifest_dir();
488	            let config = config_for_compare(
489	                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.stl", $model),
490	                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_nurbs_{}.step", $model),
491	                &format!("{dir}/tests/nurbs/{}.step", $model),
```

```bash
  laststage=$(grep -oE '^(Stage|  Compare) [0-9.]+' $log | tail -1)

  printf "%-38s rc=%-3s %-14s last=%-16s %s %s\n" "$name" "$rc" "$surf" "$laststage" "$v41" "$err"
done
```

```
/// Build a compound containing all solids.
fn build_solid_compound(solids: &[OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Solid>]) -> OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Compound> {
    let builder = topo_ds::Builder::new();
    let mut compound = topo_ds::Compound::new();
    builder.make_compound(&mut compound);
    for solid in solids {
        builder.add(compound.as_shape_mut(), solid.as_shape());
    }
    compound
}

/// Compare the (already re-read) written STEP against the reference STEP
/// shape. \`output_shape\`/\`output_vol\` come from \`verify_output\`, which read
/// the file once for both the round-trip self-check and this comparison.
fn compare_output_to_step(
    output_shape: &topo_ds::Shape,
    output_vol: f64,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<(), Stage4CompareError> {
    let compare_shape = config.compare_shape.as_ref().unwrap();

    // Compare volumes
    let ref_vol = compute_volume(compare_shape);
    let rel_diff = if ref_vol > 0.0 {
        (output_vol - ref_vol).abs() / ref_vol
    } else {
        0.0
    };

    if !config.quiet {
        eprintln!(
            "  Compare 4.1: output volume {output_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} vs STEP {ref_vol:.6} mm\u{00b3} (rel diff {rel_diff:.2e})",
        );
    }

    if rel_diff > 0.01 {
        eprintln!(
            "  Compare 4.1: ERROR volume differs by {rel_diff:.2e} (>1%)",
        );
        return Err(Stage4CompareError::Volume { rel_diff });
    }

    // Compute BRepExtrema distance between output and reference
    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
    let dist_calc = b_rep_extrema::DistShapeShape::new_shape2_extflag_extalgo_progressrange(
        output_shape,
        compare_shape,
        0,
        extrema::ExtAlgo::Grad,
        &progress,
    );
    if dist_calc.is_done() && dist_calc.nb_solution() > 0 {
        let dist = dist_calc.value();
        if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!("  Compare 4.1: output distance to STEP = {dist:.6e} mm");
        }
        if dist > config.surface_tolerance_mm {
            return Err(Stage4CompareError::Distance {
                max_distance: dist,
                tolerance: config.surface_tolerance_mm,
            });
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

fn compute_volume(shape: &topo_ds::Shape) -> f64 {
    let mut gprops = g_prop::GProps::new();
    b_rep_g_prop::volume_properties_shape_gprops_bool3(
        shape,
        &mut gprops,
        true, false, false,
    );
    gprops.mass().abs()
}
```

```
//! Integration tests for Stage 1: mesh input and validation.
//!
//! Tests that all STL/STEP test file pairs pass stage1 with consistency checks
//! and --compare validation, and that intentionally bad files fail correctly.

use brepper::config;
use brepper::stage1;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn config_for_stl(stl_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--stage=1", "-q"]).unwrap()
}

fn config_for_compare(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config =
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--compare", step_path, "--stage=1", "-q"])
            .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Macros for generating test cases
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Generate a test that runs stage1 (read + validate) on a given STL file.
macro_rules! test_stl_stage1 {
    ($name:ident, $rel_path:literal) => {
        #[test]
        fn $name() {
            let stl = format!("{}/{}", manifest_dir(), $rel_path);
            let config = config_for_stl(&stl);
            stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1 should pass");
        }
    };
}

/// Generate a test that runs stage1 with --compare against a STEP file.
macro_rules! test_stl_step_compare {
    ($name:ident, $stl_path:literal, $step_path:literal) => {
        #[test]
        fn $name() {
            let stl = format!("{}/{}", manifest_dir(), $stl_path);
            let step = format!("{}/{}", manifest_dir(), $step_path);
            let config = config_for_compare(&stl, &step);
            stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1 with --compare should pass");
        }
    };
}

    // The hollow cube has 2 closed shells; the inner one (negative signed

    assert_eq!(mesh.stats.voids_within_solids, 1, "should have 1 void");
}
```

```
//     as the binary variant, which is covered through stage 4. Its purpose is
//     the ASCII reader; pinned by `chamfered_cube_ascii_matches_binary` in
//     stage1_integration.rs rather than by a duplicate pipeline run.

macro_rules! stage41_compare {
    ($name:ident, $stl:literal, $step:literal) => {
        #[test]
        fn $name() {
            let dir = manifest_dir();
            let config = config_for_compare(
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.stl", $stl),
                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_cover_{}.step", stringify!($name)),
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.step", $step),
            );
            run_stage4(&config);
        }
    };
}
```

```
#[test]
fn chamfered_cube_ascii_matches_binary() {
    // tests/onshape/chamfered_cube_10_c1_medium.ascii.stl is the ASCII export of
    // the same body as the binary variant, and the Phase 0.1 coverage audit
    // found it referenced by no test at all. Its purpose is the ASCII reader, so
    // pin exactly that: identical topology and the same geometry, rather than a
    // duplicate run of the whole pipeline.
    //
    // The bar is 1e-4 mm because that is the ASCII file's own resolution — it
    // carries 6 significant digits ("48.0012"), coarser than the binary file's
    // float32 (~6.7e-6 mm at these coordinates). It is a file-format precision,
    // not a tolerance to tune.
    let dir = manifest_dir();
    let ascii = stage1::stage1(&config_for_stl(&format!(
        "{dir}/tests/onshape/chamfered_cube_10_c1_medium.ascii.stl"
    )))
    .expect("ASCII stage1 should pass");
    let binary = stage1::stage1(&config_for_stl(&format!(
        "{dir}/tests/onshape/chamfered_cube_10_c1_medium.stl"
    )))
    .expect("binary stage1 should pass");

    assert_eq!(ascii.vertices.len(), binary.vertices.len(), "vertex count");
    assert_eq!(ascii.faces.len(), binary.faces.len(), "face count");
    assert_eq!(ascii.stats.mesh_quads, binary.stats.mesh_quads, "quad count");
    assert_eq!(ascii.stats.solids, binary.stats.solids, "solid count");
    assert_eq!(ascii.stats.mesh_edges_open, binary.stats.mesh_edges_open, "open edges");

    // Order-independent: every ASCII vertex has a binary counterpart nearby.
    for (i, a) in ascii.vertices.iter().enumerate() {
        let best = binary
            .vertices
            .iter()
            .map(|b| ((a.x - b.x).powi(2) + (a.y - b.y).powi(2) + (a.z - b.z).powi(2)).sqrt())
            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
        assert!(
            best < 1.0e-4,
            "ASCII vertex {i} at ({}, {}, {}) is {best:.3e} mm from the nearest binary vertex",
            a.x,
            a.y,
            a.z
        );
    }
}
```

```
1	//! Generates test models that cannot be produced via ccad, using OCCT
2	//! directly. The STL/STEP pairs are written to tests/occt/ and tests/nurbs/
3	//! and committed to the repo, so this tool only needs to be re-run when a
4	//! model changes.
5	//!
6	//! Usage: gen_test_models [<occt_dir>] [<nurbs_dir>]
7	//!        (defaults: tests/occt tests/nurbs)
8	//!
9	//! tests/occt/ models (analytic, exercise the existing pipeline):
10	//! - hollow_cube: 20 mm cube with a fully enclosed 10 mm cubic void at its
11	//!   center. Exercises multi-shell solid construction: the mesh has two
12	//!   closed shells and the STEP output must be ONE solid with an internal
13	//!   cavity (volume 7000 mm³), not two nested solids.
14	//! - full_torus: complete donut (R=10, r=3). Exercises the doubly-periodic
15	//!   seam handling in stage 3.4: a complete torus face needs both a U seam
16	//!   (around the major circle) and a V seam (around the tube).
17	//!
18	//! tests/nurbs/ models (freeform, targets for the DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.7
19	//! NURBS fallback — expected to FAIL --compare until that stage exists):
20	//!
21	//! Every reference STEP is built from EXACT geometry — explicit-pole
22	//! Geom_BSplineSurface lattices, conic/B-spline extrusions, and booleans of
23	//! those. No surface is produced by fitting sampled points: the recognizer
24	//! will use OCCT's fitting APIs, so a fitted reference would be circular
25	//! (shared biases cancel) and merely approximate.
26	//!
27	//! STLs come in two styles. The doubly-curved patch models are scripted
28	//! regular grids with vertices sampled exactly on the reference surface —
29	//! the cleanest possible first inputs for a fitter. The ruled/extruded
30	//! models (elliptical_arch, elliptical_cylinder, bspline_wave) arrive as
31	//! STRIP meshes — full-length quads with NO interior vertices along the
32	//! ruling, which is how real CAD exporters tessellate extrusions — kept
33	//! deliberately so the NURBS recognizer is built against realistic strip
34	//! meshes from day one. The two conic models get their strips from genuine
35	//! OCCT tessellation; the wave's strips are scripted because BRepMesh
36	//! internally grid-refines B-spline-based surfaces (interior nodes appear
37	//! at any deflection/angle setting). hill_with_hole is a plain OCCT
38	//! tessellation: one realistically irregular CAD-export-style mesh. Every
39	//! written STL is parsed back and validated (closed oriented manifold,
40	//! volume against the B-rep).
41	//!
42	//! In roughly increasing order of recognizer difficulty:
```

```
//! This crate provides low-level FFI bindings to the OpenCASCADE geometry kernel.

//! # Structure
```

```
README.md
# CodeCAD Test Models

Test models generated by [CodeCAD](https://codecad.xyz/). The generated STL/STEP
files are committed to the repo, so CodeCAD is not required to run tests.

## Regenerating Models

\`\`\`bash
# Requires 'ccad' tool installed
./tests/ccad/generate_models.sh
\`\`\`

This runs \`ccad build\` in the \`tests/ccad/\` directory and writes
STL + STEP pairs into \`tests/ccad/generated/\`.

## CodeCAD Primitive Conventions

Full documentation: \`../codecad/docs/\` (especially \`core_primitives.md\`,
\`core_transform.md\`, \`core_boolean.md\`).

**Critical: \`box()\` places a corner at the origin, NOT centered.**

| Primitive              | Placement                                  |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| \`box(w, d, h)\`         | Corner at origin, extends into +x/+y/+z   |
| \`cylinder(diameter, h)\` | Centered in x/y, z from 0 to h            |
| \`sphere(diameter)\`     | Centered at origin                         |
| \`cone(d1, d2, h)\`     | Centered in x/y, z from 0 to h            |
| \`wedge(dx, dy, dz, ltx)\` | Corner at origin                        |

To center a box at the origin, use \`center_xyz(box(w, d, h))\`.
Other centering helpers: \`center_x()\`, \`center_y()\`, \`center_z()\`,
\`center_xy()\`, \`center_to(s, cx, cy, cz)\`.

## Analytical Values

Every part's \`.lua\` file has comments near the top giving the expected
analytical surface area and volume. When writing tests or debugging surface
reconstruction, **use these values** from the lua file comments rather than
computing them from scratch.
```

```
174	    /// bypassing \`tri\`'s zero-area filter, so closure checks see exactly
175	    /// what was written).
176	    fn from_stl_file(path: &str) -> Self {
177	        let data = std::fs::read(path).expect("failed to read back STL");
178	        assert!(data.len() >= 84, "{path}: truncated binary STL");
179	        let n = u32::from_le_bytes(data[80..84].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
180	        assert_eq!(data.len(), 84 + 50 * n, "{path}: bad binary STL length");
181	        let mut tris = Vec::with_capacity(n);
182	        for t in 0..n {
183	            let base = 84 + 50 * t + 12; // skip the stored normal
184	            let mut tri = [[0.0f64; 3]; 3];
185	            for (v, corner) in tri.iter_mut().enumerate() {
186	                for (c, coord) in corner.iter_mut().enumerate() {
187	                    let off = base + 12 * v + 4 * c;
188	                    *coord = f32::from_le_bytes(data[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as f64;
189	                }
190	            }
191	            tris.push(tri);
192	        }
193	        MeshBuf { tris }
194	    }
195	
196	    fn tri(&mut self, a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3], c: [f64; 3]) {
197	        let u = [b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2]];
198	        let v = [c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2]];
199	        let n = cross(u, v);
200	        // Chain-merged triangulations legitimately emit zero-area triangles
201	        // where two chains share a vertex; drop them.
202	        if norm(n) < 1e-12 {
203	            return;
204	        }
205	        self.tris.push([a, b, c]);
206	    }
207	
208	    /// Quad split into two triangles; \`alt\` flips the diagonal so grid
209	    /// meshes alternate diagonals checkerboard-style.
210	    fn quad(&mut self, a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3], c: [f64; 3], d: [f64; 3], alt: bool) {
211	        if alt {
212	            self.tri(b, c, d);
213	            self.tri(b, d, a);
214	        } else {
215	            self.tri(a, b, c);
216	            self.tri(a, c, d);
217	        }
218	    }
219	
220	    /// Signed volume via the divergence theorem. Positive for a closed mesh
221	    /// with outward-facing normals.
222	    fn volume(&self) -> f64 {
223	        let mut v6 = 0.0;
224	        for t in &self.tris {
225	            v6 += dot(t[0], cross(t[1], t[2]));
226	        }
227	        v6 / 6.0
228	    }
229	
230	    /// Every directed edge must be matched by its reverse exactly once.
231	    /// Catches open boundaries, T-junctions, duplicated and flipped faces.
232	    fn assert_closed_manifold(&self, name: &str) {
233	        let mut edges: HashMap<([u64; 3], [u64; 3]), i64> = HashMap::new();
234	        for t in &self.tris {
235	            for (p, q) in [(t[0], t[1]), (t[1], t[2]), (t[2], t[0])] {
236	                let (kp, kq) = (vkey(p), vkey(q));
237	                // A zero-length edge (two corners rounding to the same f32
238	                // triple in a parsed STL) pairs with nothing; skip it — the
239	                // sliver's remaining edges still participate in closure.
240	                if kp == kq {
241	                    continue;
242	                }
243	                // +1 in lexicographically increasing direction, -1 reverse.
244	                if kp < kq {
245	                    *edges.entry((kp, kq)).or_insert(0) += 1;
246	                } else {
247	                    *edges.entry((kq, kp)).or_insert(0) -= 1;
248	                }
249	            }
250	        }
251	        let bad = edges.values().filter(|&&c| c != 0).count();
252	        assert_eq!(bad, 0, "{name}: mesh is not a closed oriented manifold ({bad} unmatched edges)");
253	    }
254	
255	    fn write_stl(&self, dir: &str, name: &str) {
256	        let path = format!("{dir}/{name}.stl");
257	        let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(84 + 50 * self.tris.len());
258	        let mut header = [0u8; 80];
259	        let tag = b"brepper gen-test-models scripted mesh";
260	        header[..tag.len()].copy_from_slice(tag);
261	        buf.extend_from_slice(&header);
262	        buf.extend_from_slice(&(self.tris.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
263	        for t in &self.tris {
264	            let u = [t[1][0] - t[0][0], t[1][1] - t[0][1], t[1][2] - t[0][2]];
265	            let v = [t[2][0] - t[0][0], t[2][1] - t[0][1], t[2][2] - t[0][2]];
266	            let mut n = cross(u, v);
267	            let len = norm(n);
268	            n = [n[0] / len, n[1] / len, n[2] / len];
269	            for x in n {
270	                buf.extend_from_slice(&(x as f32).to_le_bytes());
271	            }
272	            for p in t {
273	                for x in p {
274	                    buf.extend_from_slice(&(*x as f32).to_le_bytes());
275	                }
276	            }
277	            buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes());
278	        }
279	        std::fs::write(&path, buf).expect("failed to write STL");
280	        println!("wrote {path} ({} triangles)", self.tris.len());
281	    }
282	}
283	
284	fn cross(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
285	    [
286	        a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1],
287	        a[2] * b[0] - a[0] * b[2],
288	        a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0],
```

```
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Re-mesh mode (Phase 0.2)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// `gen_test_models remesh [<out_dir>] [<step> ...]` loads existing reference
// STEPs and re-tessellates them with OCCT's BRepMesh at several densities,
// writing STLs next to a copy of the reference each `--compare` run needs.
//
// Why: the corpus is Parasolid-heavy (Onshape exports), and Parasolid
// tessellates by sweeping STRIPS — full-length quads with no interior
// vertices along a ruling. BRepMesh is constrained Delaunay instead, which
// breaks two properties the pipeline has quietly been able to rely on: a
// facet no longer spans two rulings of a cylinder (so a facet normal is no
// longer exactly perpendicular to the axis — the Phase 1.1 initializer
// caveat), and facets are no longer grid-aligned (so meridian normals on a
// torus are only approximate). Re-meshing the SAME references keeps the
// ground truth exact while changing only the provenance.
//
// Off-origin variants exist to make the float32 quantum testable. An STL
// stores coordinates as f32, so vertex precision is a *relative* quantity:
// max|coordinate| * 1.19e-7. At the origin-centred corpus sizes that is
// ~1e-6 mm; translated a metre away it is ~1e-4 mm, which is larger than the
// 5e-5 mm default --vertex-tolerance. Both the STL and a translated copy of
// the reference STEP are written so --compare still applies.

/// Tessellation settings for the re-mesh variants. These are inputs to the
/// mesh GENERATOR, not pipeline tolerances: they describe what a CAD exporter
/// was asked for, exactly as Onshape's coarse/medium/fine presets do.
/// Deflection is chordal deviation in mm; the angle bounds the turn between
/// adjacent facets.
const REMESH_DENSITIES: &[(&str, f64, f64)] = &[
    ("coarse", 0.5, 30.0),
    ("medium", 0.1, 15.0),
    ("fine", 0.02, 6.0),
];

/// Translation for the off-origin variants, ~1 m in length. Deliberately not
/// uniform across the axes and deliberately leaving z near the origin: the
/// f32 quantum of a *distance* is direction-weighted, so a part that is far
/// away in x and y but not in z is the informative case — and it is also what
/// a part positioned inside a real assembly looks like.
const REMESH_OFFSET: [f64; 3] = [600.0, 800.0, 0.0];

/// Reference STEPs re-meshed by default. Chosen for surface-type coverage
/// (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, fillet networks, graded plane/hole pairs)
/// among models whose current STLs are all Parasolid strips.
const REMESH_MODELS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("tests/onshape/cylinder_10x30.step", "cylinder_10x30"),
    ("tests/onshape/sphere_25.step", "sphere_25"),
    ("tests/onshape/pill.step", "pill"),
    ("tests/onshape/plate_with_hole_100x50.step", "plate_with_hole_100x50"),
    ("tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2.step", "rounded_cube_10_r2"),
    ("tests/onshape/cone_tangent_planes.step", "cone_tangent_planes"),
    ("tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10.step", "pipe_elbow_10"),
    ("tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets.step", "stepped_block_toroidal"),
];

/// Tessellate `shape` at (deflection, angle) and write `<dir>/<name>.stl`,
/// then read it back and report closure, volume error against the B-rep, and
/// the f32 quantum implied by its coordinates.
fn write_remesh_variant(
    shape: &topo_ds::Shape,
    dir: &str,
    name: &str,
    deflection: f64,
    angle_deg: f64,
    brep_vol: f64,
) {
    // BRepMesh is *incremental*: it reuses any triangulation already cached on
    // the shape. Clean first or the second density silently returns the first.
    b_rep_tools::clean(shape, true);
    write_tessellated_stl(shape, dir, name, deflection, angle_deg);

    let mesh = MeshBuf::from_stl_file(&format!("{dir}/{name}.stl"));
    mesh.assert_closed_manifold(name);
    let vol = mesh.volume();
    let rel = (vol - brep_vol).abs() / brep_vol;
    let max_coord = mesh
        .tris
        .iter()
        .flatten()
        .flatten()
        .fold(0.0f64, |m, c| m.max(c.abs()));
    println!(
        "  {name}: {} tris, volume {vol:.4} vs B-rep {brep_vol:.4} (rel {rel:.2e}), \
         max|coord| {max_coord:.1} mm -> f32 quantum {:.2e} mm",
        mesh.tris.len(),
        max_coord * 1.192_092_9e-7,
    );
}

/// Re-mesh one reference STEP at every density, plus an off-origin variant.
fn remesh_model(out_dir: &str, step_path: &str, name: &str) {
    let shape = read_step_file(step_path)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("failed to read {step_path}: {e}"));
    let brep_vol = shape_volume(&shape).abs();
    println!("remeshing {step_path} (B-rep volume {brep_vol:.4} mm³)");

    for (label, deflection, angle) in REMESH_DENSITIES {
        write_remesh_variant(
            &shape,
            out_dir,
            &format!("{name}_occt_{label}"),
            *deflection,
            *angle,
            brep_vol,
        );
    }

    // Off-origin: a translated reference STEP plus one medium tessellation of
    // it. Copy the geometry (rather than only setting a location) so the
    // written STEP carries genuinely translated surfaces.
    let mut trsf = gp::Trsf::new();
    let offset = gp::Vec::new_real3(REMESH_OFFSET[0], REMESH_OFFSET[1], REMESH_OFFSET[2]);
    trsf.set_translation_part(&offset);
    let mut xform = b_rep_builder_api::Transform::new_shape_trsf_bool(&shape, &trsf, true);
    let moved_name = format!("{name}_offset");
    {
        let moved = xform.as_modify_shape_mut().shape();
        write_step(moved, out_dir, &moved_name);
    }
    let moved = xform.as_modify_shape_mut().shape();
    let (_, deflection, angle) = REMESH_DENSITIES[1];
    write_remesh_variant(
        moved,
        out_dir,
        &format!("{moved_name}_occt_medium"),
        deflection,
        angle,
        brep_vol,
    );
}

fn remesh_corpus(out_dir: &str, models: &[(String, String)]) {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir).expect("failed to create remesh output dir");
    for (step_path, name) in models {
        remesh_model(out_dir, step_path, name);
    }
}
```

```bash
#!/bin/zsh
# Full pipeline over the OCCT re-mesh variants.
cd .
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sethml-src-brepper/e3a3f0cb-dd9a-4629-bc2b-e791d60d63ad/scratchpad
R=$SP/remesh
mkdir -p $SP/rlogs
models=(
  "cylinder_10x30:tests/onshape/cylinder_10x30.step"
  "sphere_25:tests/onshape/sphere_25.step"
  "pill:tests/onshape/pill.step"
  "plate_with_hole_100x50:tests/onshape/plate_with_hole_100x50.step"
  "rounded_cube_10_r2:tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2.step"
  "cone_tangent_planes:tests/onshape/cone_tangent_planes.step"
  "pipe_elbow_10:tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10.step"
  "stepped_block_toroidal:tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets.step"
)
for entry in $models; do
  m=${entry%%:*}; ref=${entry##*:}
  for v in occt_coarse occt_medium occt_fine offset_occt_medium; do
    stl=$R/${m}_${v}.stl
    [ -f $stl ] || continue
    r=$ref
    [[ $v == offset* ]] && r=$R/${m}_offset.step
    log=$SP/rlogs/${m}_${v}.log
    ./target/release/brepper $stl -o $SP/rlogs/${m}_${v}.step --compare $r >$log 2>&1
    rc=$?
    surf=$(./target/release/dump_regions $stl surfaces 2>/dev/null \
        | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="plane")p++; else if($i=="cyl")c++; else if($i=="cone")k++;
                else if($i=="sphere")s++; else if($i=="torus")t++; else if($i=="bspline")b++}
               END{printf "%d/%d/%d/%d/%d/%d", p+0,c+0,k+0,s+0,t+0,b+0}')
    nsurf=$(echo $surf | tr '/' '+' | bc)
    fail=$(grep -oE "(Stage|Compare) [0-9.]+:? *(ERROR|WARNING).*" $log | head -1 | cut -c1-95)
    [ -z "$fail" ] && fail=$(grep -iE "^Error" $log | head -1 | cut -c1-95)
    t=$(grep -oE 'Total CPU time: [0-9.]+' $log | grep -oE '[0-9.]+')
    printf "%-24s %-18s rc=%d %-14s n=%-4s %5ss  %s\n" "$m" "$v" "$rc" "$surf" "$nsurf" "$t" "$fail"
  done
done

```

````markdown
# OCCT re-meshes of existing references (Phase 0.2)

Generated by `gen-test-models remesh` — see the "Re-mesh mode" section of
`src/bin/gen_test_models.rs` for the settings and the reasoning. Regenerate
with:

```bash
cargo run --release --bin gen-test-models -- remesh tests/remesh
```

The mesh output is deterministic: re-running produces byte-identical STLs.
The `*_offset.step` files differ only in the timestamp OCCT embeds in the
STEP header, exactly as the other committed reference STEPs do.

## What these add

Every model here is a **re-tessellation of a reference STEP that already
exists elsewhere in `tests/`**, so the ground truth is unchanged and *only the
mesh provenance* varies. Two properties change, both of which the pipeline had
quietly been able to rely on:

* **Constrained Delaunay instead of strips.** The Onshape (Parasolid) exports
  tessellate a swept surface as full-length quads with no interior vertices
  along the ruling. OCCT's `BRepMesh` produces Delaunay triangles instead. A
  facet therefore no longer spans two rulings of a cylinder, so its normal is
  no longer exactly perpendicular to the axis, and facets are not grid-aligned,
  so torus meridian normals are only approximate. Both are load-bearing
  assumptions for the Phase 1 closed-form initializers.
* **Off-origin coordinates.** An STL stores f32, so vertex precision is
  relative: `max|coordinate| × 1.19e-7`. The `*_offset*` variants are
  translated ~1 m (600, 800, 0 mm), which raises the quantum from ~3e-6 mm to
  ~1e-4 mm — past the 5e-5 mm default `--vertex-tolerance`.

## Naming

* `<model>_occt_{coarse,medium,fine}.stl` — deflection 0.5 / 0.1 / 0.02 mm at
  30° / 15° / 6°. Compare against the ORIGINAL reference (e.g.
  `tests/onshape/cylinder_10x30.step`); no copy is kept here.
* `<model>_offset_occt_medium.stl` + `<model>_offset.step` — the medium
  settings applied to the translated body, with its own translated reference.

## Measured at generation time (2026-07-29)

| model | coarse | medium | fine | offset quantum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cylinder_10x30 | 92 tris | 188 | 476 | 9.60e-5 mm |
| sphere_25 | 304 | 1256 | 7302 | 9.69e-5 mm |
| pill | 398 | 1354 | 7790 | 9.56e-5 mm |
| plate_with_hole_100x50 | 112 | 208 | 496 | 9.54e-5 mm |
| rounded_cube_10_r2 | 580 | 1668 | 8676 | 9.54e-5 mm |
| cone_tangent_planes | 202 | 544 | 2392 | 9.41e-5 mm |
| pipe_elbow_10 | 524 | 1820 | 9356 | 1.02e-4 mm |
| stepped_block_toroidal | 1948 | 6464 | 35596 | 8.77e-5 mm |

Every mesh is a closed oriented manifold; tessellation volume error runs from
7.3e-6 (fine plate) to 4.65e-2 (coarse sphere) relative.

**The off-origin meshes pass stage 1 `--compare` with 2.7e-5 to 4.2e-5 mm max
vertex-to-surface distance** — under the 5e-5 default, but only just, and
about 0.42× their own quantum. The quantum bounds a coordinate error; the
distance to the surface is that error projected onto the normal, so half a
quantum is the operative figure. At ~800 mm from the origin the default
vertex tolerance therefore has under 20% margin, and a part positioned a few
metres out in an assembly would break it. That is what Phase 0.6's clamp is
for.

## Status against the reference (see tests/stage4_integration.rs)

24 of the 32 pass end-to-end `--compare`. The 8 that fail are all real
findings, not corpus defects, and carry precise blockers in the suite:

* `stepped_block_toroidal` fails at **every** density including fine, while
  the Parasolid fine mesh of the same body passes at exactly 71 surfaces. The
  18 tori are found every time; the planes and cylinders around them
  fragment (88 surfaces at medium, 97 at fine). This is the single most
  valuable row in this directory: it is the strip assumption showing up as a
  measurable failure rather than as a suspicion.
* Coarse `sphere_25`, `rounded_cube_10_r2` and `cone_tangent_planes` fail;
  their medium and fine variants pass.

````

```
    ($name:ident, $stl:literal, $step:literal) => {

            let dir = manifest_dir();
            let config = config_for_compare(
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.stl", $stl),
                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_cover_{}.step", stringify!($name)),
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.step", $step),
```

```
            let dir = manifest_dir();
            let config = config_for_compare(
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.stl", $stl),
                &format!("{dir}/tmp/test_cover_{}.step", stringify!($name)),
                &format!("{dir}/tests/{}.step", $step),
            );
            run_stage4(&config);
        }
    };
}
```

> The current test script has the pairing logic and special-flags hook, but it's serial and its find_step function doesn't handle remesh models properly—it strips suffixes like `_fine` but then fails to match the base name. The sweep harness needs to extend that pairing logic to account for remesh variants, run jobs in parallel, and output machine-readable rows with per-type breakdowns and error data.
> 
> I'll write `tools/sweep.sh` as a self-contained bash script with an enhanced `find_step` that handles remesh naming patterns (stripping `_occt_<density>` and `_offset_occt_<density>` suffixes, plus an exceptions table for mismatches like `stepped_block_toroidal` → `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets`). I'll also move `tmp/probe.sh` to `tools/probe.sh` as noted. The script will use a self-call pattern with `--one <stl>` so `xargs -P` can parallelize across models, and output TSV rows with columns for model, status, shape counts by type, edge distance, volume error, runtime, and notes—making it easy to diff and parse with standard tools.
> 
> For status tracking, I'm adding a separate `ref` column to indicate whether a baseline exists (`step`, `none`), keeping status itself simple as `ok`, `fail`, or `timeout`. Baseline diffing will compare rows by model, flagging changes in status, counts, and metrics using a relative epsilon (>1% for edge/volume, any change for counts/status), and >30% for runtime since it's noisy. I'll set the timeout to 600 seconds per model since the largest cases like 3DBenchy can be slow, and I need to check whether `timeout` is available on macOS since `run_test_table.sh` already uses it.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# The sweep harness (Phase 0.3): every corpus model through the full pipeline
# with --compare, one machine-readable row per model, with baseline save/diff.
#
# This is the instrument the Robustness Rework is measured with. It replaces
# eyeballing tools/probe.sh output on 14 hand-picked models. See TODO.md
# ("Measurement protocol") and DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md ("The Robustness Rework").
#
# Usage:
#   tools/sweep.sh [--out FILE] [--jobs N] [--filter REGEX] [--timeout SECS]
#   tools/sweep.sh --baseline [FILE]   run, then save the result as the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff [FILE]       run, then diff against the baseline
#   tools/sweep.sh --diff-only A B     diff two existing result files
#   tools/sweep.sh --list              print the model/reference pairing and exit
#
# Defaults: --out tmp/sweep.tsv, --jobs 8, --timeout 600, baseline
# tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv (tmp/ is gitignored, so baselines stay local).
#
# Output is TSV with a '#'-comment header. Columns:
#   model    path under tests/, without the .stl extension
#   status   ok | fail | timeout
#   ref      step (compared against a reference) | none (crash-test only)
#   n        total surfaces in the final selection
#   plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline    per-type breakdown
#   edge_mm  stage 3.1 max edge-boundary distance to the reference
#   vol_rel  stage 4.1 output-volume relative error
#   secs     wall time
#   note     first error line, or empty
#
# RUNTIME CAVEAT: with --jobs > 1 the secs column is inflated by contention.
# Use --jobs 1 for any runtime measurement (Phase 2). The header records the
# job count so a diff cannot silently compare the two.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BREPPER=./target/release/brepper
OUT=tmp/sweep.tsv
JOBS=8
FILTER=""
TIMEOUT=600
BASELINE=tmp/sweep-baseline.tsv
MODE=run

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model/reference pairing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Rules, in order. Anything that falls through runs without --compare and is
# reported as ref=none, which is correct for crash-test-only inputs but is
# also how a new model with a perfectly good reference could go unmeasured —
# so `--list` prints the pairing for review.

find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir base stripped
    dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # Name mismatches that no rule can derive. Keep this list short; prefer
    # naming a generated model after its reference.
    case "$base" in
        stepped_block_toroidal_occt_*)
            echo "tests/onshape/stepped_block_toroidal_fillets.step"; return ;;
    esac

    # tests/remesh: <model>_offset_occt_<density> pairs with the translated
    # reference next to it; <model>_occt_<density> with the original reference,
    # which lives in another directory.
    if [[ "$base" == *_offset_occt_* ]]; then
        local off="${base%_occt_*}"
        [ -f "$dir/$off.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$off.step"; return; }
    fi
    if [[ "$base" == *_occt_* ]]; then
        local model="${base%_occt_*}"
        local hit
        hit=$(find tests -name "$model.step" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)
        [ -n "$hit" ] && { echo "$hit"; return; }
    fi

    base="${base%.ascii}"
    [ -f "$dir/$base.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$base.step"; return; }

    stripped=$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/_(coarse|medium|fine|low|high)$//')
    [ -f "$dir/$stripped.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$stripped.step"; return; }

    echo ""
}

# Per-model CLI flags, mirroring tests/RESULTS.md's "Special flags".
extra_flags() {
    case "$1" in
        *rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse*) echo "--angular-tolerance 20" ;;
        *) echo "" ;;
    esac
}

# Every STL under tests/ except:
#   bad/         inputs that must FAIL; the suite pins their exact errors
#   *.ascii.stl  duplicate geometry, pinned by a reader test instead
model_list() {
    find tests -name '*.stl' \
        -not -path 'tests/bad/*' \
        -not -name '*.ascii.stl' \
    | sort \
    | { [ -n "$FILTER" ] && grep -E "$FILTER" || cat; }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_one() {
    local stl="$1"
    local model="${stl#tests/}"; model="${model%.stl}"
    local step flags log outstep start end secs rc
    step=$(find_step "$stl")
    flags=$(extra_flags "$stl")
    log=$(mktemp); outstep="$log.step"

    start=$(date +%s.%N)
    if [ -n "$step" ]; then
        timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$BREPPER" "$stl" -o "$outstep" --compare "$step" -v $flags \
            >"$log" 2>&1
    else
        timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$BREPPER" "$stl" -o "$outstep" -v $flags >"$log" 2>&1
    fi
    rc=$?
    end=$(date +%s.%N)
    secs=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.2f\", $end - $start}")

    local status=ok
    [ $rc -eq 0 ] || status=fail
    [ $rc -eq 124 ] && status=timeout

    # "Stage 2 types: 2 plane, 2 cyl, 0 cone, 0 sphere, 4 torus, 0 bspline (8 total)"
    local types
    types=$(grep -m1 '^Stage 2 types:' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/^Stage 2 types: ([0-9]+) plane, ([0-9]+) cyl, ([0-9]+) cone, ([0-9]+) sphere, ([0-9]+) torus, ([0-9]+) bspline \(([0-9]+) total\)/\7\t\1\t\2\t\3\t\4\t\5\t\6/')
    [ -n "$types" ] || types=$(printf -- '-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-')

    local edge vol note
    edge=$(grep -m1 'Compare 3.1: edge boundary max dist' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/.*max dist ([0-9.e+-]+) mm.*/\1/')
    [ -n "$edge" ] || edge=-
    vol=$(grep -m1 'Compare 4.1: output volume' "$log" \
        | sed -E 's/.*rel diff ([0-9.e+-]+)\).*/\1/')
    [ -n "$vol" ] || vol=-
    note=""
    if [ "$status" != ok ]; then
        note=$(grep -m1 -iE '^Error|panicked at' "$log" | tr '\t' ' ' | cut -c1-160)
        [ "$status" = timeout ] && note="timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s"
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$model" "$status" "$([ -n "$step" ] && echo step || echo none)" \
        "$types" "$edge" "$vol" "$secs" "$note"
    rm -f "$log" "$outstep"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diff
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Counts and status are compared exactly; edge/vol only when they move by more
# than 1% (they are floating-point measurements, not identities). Runtime is
# reported at >50% because it is noisy, and never across differing job counts.

diff_results() {
    local old="$1" new="$2"
    [ -f "$old" ] || { echo "no baseline at $old" >&2; return 2; }
    local oj nj
    oj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$old" | awk '{print $3}')
    nj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$new" | awk '{print $3}')
    awk -v OLD="$old" -v oj="$oj" -v nj="$nj" '
        function num(x) { return (x == "-" ? -1 : x + 0) }
        BEGIN {
            FS = OFS = "\t"
            while ((getline line < OLD) > 0) {
                if (line ~ /^#/) continue
                split(line, f, FS)
                o[f[1]] = line
            }
            changed = 0
        }
        /^#/ { next }
        {
            key = $1
            if (!(key in o)) { print "NEW    ", key, $2, $4; changed++; next }
            split(o[key], b, FS)
            seen[key] = 1
            msg = ""
            if (b[2] != $2) msg = msg sprintf(" status %s->%s", b[2], $2)
            for (i = 4; i <= 10; i++)
                if (b[i] != $i) msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", hdr[i], b[i], $i)
            for (i = 11; i <= 12; i++) {
                ob = num(b[i]); nb = num($i)
                if ((ob < 0) != (nb < 0) || (ob > 0 && nb > 0 && \
                    (nb > ob * 1.01 || nb < ob * 0.99)))
                    msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", hdr[i], b[i], $i)
            }
            if (oj == nj) {
                ob = num(b[13]); nb = num($13)
                if (ob > 0.5 && (nb > ob * 1.5 || nb < ob / 1.5))
                    msg = msg sprintf(" secs %s->%s", b[13], $13)
            }
            if (msg != "") { printf "CHANGED %s:%s\n", key, msg; changed++ }
        }
        END {
            for (key in o) {
                if (!(key in seen)) {
                    split(o[key], b, FS)
                    print "GONE   ", key, b[2]
                    changed++
                }
            }
            if (changed == 0) print "no changes vs baseline"
            else printf "%d model(s) changed\n", changed
        }
        function hdr(i) { return i }
    ' \
    <(awk 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="\t"}{print}' "$new") \
    | sed -e 's/ 4 / n /' -e 's/ 5 / plane /' -e 's/ 6 / cyl /' -e 's/ 7 / cone /' \
          -e 's/ 8 / sphere /' -e 's/ 9 / torus /' -e 's/ 10 / bspline /' \
          -e 's/ 11 / edge_mm /' -e 's/ 12 / vol_rel /'
    if [ "$oj" != "$nj" ]; then
        echo "(runtime not compared: baseline ran with jobs=$oj, this run jobs=$nj)"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --out) OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --jobs) JOBS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --filter) FILTER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --timeout) TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --baseline) MODE=baseline; [ $# -ge 2 ] && [[ "$2" != --* ]] && { BASELINE="$2"; shift; }; shift ;;
        --diff) MODE=diff; [ $# -ge 2 ] && [[ "$2" != --* ]] && { BASELINE="$2"; shift; }; shift ;;
        --diff-only) diff_results "$2" "$3"; exit $? ;;
        --list) MODE=list; shift ;;
        --one) shift; run_one "$1"; exit 0 ;;   # internal: one model, for xargs
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,32p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

if [ "$MODE" = list ]; then
    while read -r stl; do
        printf '%-58s %s\n' "${stl#tests/}" "$(find_step "$stl" || echo '(no reference)')"
    done < <(model_list)
    exit 0
fi

[ -x "$BREPPER" ] || { echo "build first: cargo build --release" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"

export -f run_one find_step extra_flags
export BREPPER TIMEOUT

count=$(model_list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
{
    echo "# brepper sweep $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "# commit $(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)$(git diff --quiet 2>/dev/null || echo '-dirty')"
    echo "# jobs $JOBS   models $count   timeout ${TIMEOUT}s"
    printf '#model\tstatus\tref\tn\tplane\tcyl\tcone\tsphere\ttorus\tbspline\tedge_mm\tvol_rel\tsecs\tnote\n'
    model_list | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash "$0" --one {} | sort
} > "$OUT"

echo "wrote $OUT" >&2
awk -F'\t' '!/^#/{ n[$2]++ } END { for (s in n) printf "%s: %d\n", s, n[s] }' "$OUT" >&2

case "$MODE" in
    baseline) cp "$OUT" "$BASELINE"; echo "baseline saved to $BASELINE" >&2 ;;
    diff)     diff_results "$BASELINE" "$OUT" ;;
esac

```

```bash
diff_results() {
    local old="$1" new="$2"
    [ -f "$old" ] || { echo "no baseline at $old" >&2; return 2; }
    local oj nj
    oj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$old" | awk '{print $3}')
    nj=$(grep -m1 '^# jobs' "$new" | awk '{print $3}')
    awk -v OLD="$old" -v same_jobs="$([ "$oj" = "$nj" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" '
        function num(x) { return (x == "-" ? -1 : x + 0) }
        # A measurement moved if one side is missing or they differ by >1%.
        function moved(a, b,   x, y) {
            x = num(a); y = num(b)
            if ((x < 0) != (y < 0)) return 1
            if (x < 0) return 0
            return (y > x * 1.01 || y < x * 0.99)
        }
        BEGIN {
            FS = OFS = "\t"
            split("model status ref n plane cyl cone sphere torus bspline " \
                  "edge_mm vol_rel secs note", name, " ")
            while ((getline line < OLD) > 0) {
                if (line ~ /^#/) continue
                split(line, f, FS)
                base[f[1]] = line
            }
        }
        /^#/ { next }
        {
            key = $1
            if (!(key in base)) { printf "NEW      %s (%s, n=%s)\n", key, $2, $4; changed++; next }
            split(base[key], b, FS)
            seen[key] = 1
            msg = ""
            # Status and the integer counts are identities: any change matters.
            for (i = 2; i <= 10; i++)
                if (b[i] != $i) msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", name[i], b[i], $i)
            for (i = 11; i <= 12; i++)
                if (moved(b[i], $i)) msg = msg sprintf(" %s %s->%s", name[i], b[i], $i)
            # Runtime is noisy: only large moves, and never across job counts.
            if (same_jobs && num(b[13]) > 0.5 && \
                (num($13) > num(b[13]) * 1.5 || num($13) < num(b[13]) / 1.5))
                msg = msg sprintf(" secs %s->%s", b[13], $13)
            if (msg != "") { printf "CHANGED  %s:%s\n", key, msg; changed++ }
        }
        END {
            for (key in base)
                if (!(key in seen)) {
                    split(base[key], b, FS)
                    printf "GONE     %s (was %s)\n", key, b[2]
                    changed++
                }
            if (changed == 0) print "no changes vs baseline"
            else printf "%d model(s) changed\n", changed
        }
    ' "$new"
    if [ "$oj" != "$nj" ]; then
        echo "(runtime not compared: baseline ran with jobs=$oj, this run jobs=$nj)"
    fi
}
```

```
fn remesh_corpus(out_dir: &str, models: &[(String, String)]) {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir).expect("failed to create remesh output dir");
    for (step_path, name) in models {
        remesh_model(out_dir, step_path, name);
    }

    // Record which reference each model came from. A re-mesh's reference lives
    // in another directory, and guessing it by searching tests/ for a matching
    // stem is ambiguous (plate_with_hole_100x50.step exists under both
    // fusion/ and onshape/) and filesystem-order dependent. tools/sweep.sh
    // reads this file, so the pairing is recorded rather than inferred.
    let manifest: String = models
        .iter()
        .map(|(step_path, name)| format!("{name}\t{step_path}\n"))
        .collect();
    let path = format!("{out_dir}/sources.tsv");
    std::fs::write(&path, format!("# model\treference STEP it was tessellated from\n{manifest}"))
        .expect("failed to write remesh sources manifest");
    println!("wrote {path}");
}
```
</details>

**After:**
```bash
    # tests/remesh: <model>_offset_occt_<density> pairs with the translated
    # reference written next to it; <model>_occt_<density> with the original
    # reference in another directory, which tests/remesh/sources.tsv records
    # (the generator writes it — do not guess by searching for a matching stem,

    if [[ "$base" == *_offset_occt_* ]]; then

        [ -f "$dir/$off.step" ] && { echo "$dir/$off.step"; return; }
    fi
    if [[ "$base" == *_occt_* && -f tests/remesh/sources.tsv ]]; then
        local model="${base%_occt_*}" hit
        hit=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$model" '$1 == m { print $2; exit }' tests/remesh/sources.tsv)
```

> I'm noticing the harness output has a formatting issue where the `note` column is breaking across multiple lines instead of staying contained. The error messages are appearing as separate sorted rows starting with "Error:" rather than being embedded in the note field, which suggests a newline character is being inserted before the note content during the printf operation.
> 
> Looking at the format string, there are 7 `%s` specifiers but 8 arguments being passed (model, status, ref, types as a single tab-delimited string, edge, vol, secs, and note). This causes printf to recycle the format string for the 8th argument, printing the note on a new line instead of in the correct column. The fix is straightforward: add an 8th `%s` placeholder to the format string.
> 
> For the second issue, the 3DBenchy timeout at 600 seconds is slowing down the sweep considerably — with 8 parallel jobs, it's taking about 15 minutes mostly waiting on that one model. I'm thinking about reducing the default timeout to 300 seconds and handling 3DBenchy as a special case that exceeds the limit, marking it as "timeout" in the results.
> 
> The bspline models are also slow — bspline_hill at 284 seconds, bspline_saddle at 251 seconds, and bspline_terrain at 213 seconds — so they'll dominate the overall wall time regardless.
> 
> There's also a mysterious blank status line appearing at the top of the summary showing `: 94`. I'm trying to figure out where that's coming from — it looks like it might be related to how the awk script is counting status values, possibly picking up something unexpected from the header or note lines. Ah, I see it now — the printf format string is recycling. When there are more arguments than format specifiers, printf loops back through the format string with the remaining arguments. So each model line gets printed with 7 specifiers consuming the first 7 arguments, then the format recycles with just the note argument left, producing a second line with mostly empty fields.
> 
> For models with no note, that's just 6 tabs and a newline — which explains the 94 extra blank rows. Fixing the printf format should resolve this.
> 
> I should also verify the note extraction is stripping tabs properly, which it is. Now looking at the specific failures: `downloaded/OrcaCube v2` is failing the vertex comparison at stage 1.2 because the STL and STEP files are different revisions or the mesh is decimated, and `nurbs/bspline_hill` passes but with a volume relative error of 4.93e-3, which is within the 1% threshold but worth noting.
> 
> Some models are taking a long time — `ccad/generated/cone_cylinder` at 43 seconds, `filleted_pipe` at 26 seconds, and `filleted_cylinder` at 20 seconds. I need to fix the printf bug, lower the default timeout to 300 seconds, and re-run the sweep while tracking total wall time to see how long it takes end-to-end. The TSV format handles spaces in filenames fine with xargs, so that's not an issue.
